value: Jane completed her studies at Queen's Academy.
unit: Jane grew up in Avonlea as part of the Andrews family and attended the local school under Mr. Phillips and later Miss Stacy. She joined Anne Shirley's story club, though she preferred writing sensible stories without romance. Jane joined the Queen's class, passed her Entrance examination calmly, and completed her studies at Queen's Academy, earning honors in domestic science. After graduating, she accepted a position as a teacher in Newbridge, where she maintained order strictly and earned a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor. She active participated in the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, serving on fundraising and petition committees. After her successful term at Newbridge, she was tipped to take over the school in Avonlea.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the trustees
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the trustees as the first female teacher at Avonlea school. She introduced novel educational practices, including morning and evening physical culture exercises, nature study field afternoons, composition practice, and biweekly recitation afternoons. In late autumn, she organized a Christmas Night school concert to fund a schoolhouse flag. She later formed an advanced class to prepare willing students for the entrance examination to Queen's Academy, giving them an extra hour of instruction after school. Though offered a job in her home district, she chose to stay in Avonlea for a second year to see her students through their Entrance exams. After successfully guiding all her Queen's class candidates through the examination in Charlottetown, her rule at Avonlea school came to an end at the close of June. She was later invited to dinner at Green Gables alongside the Allans during a visit back to Avonlea.

I think when I grow up I’ll be a trained nurse and go with the Red Crosses to the field of battle as a messenger of mercy. That is, if I don’t go out as a foreign missionary. passages.v01:c24:p0010: But all the field afternoons and recitation Fridays and physical culture contortions paled before a project which Miss Stacy brought forward in November. This was that the scholars of Avonlea school should get up a concert and hold it in the hall on Christmas Night, for the laudable purpose of helping to pay for a schoolhouse flag. label: History
value: Marilla faced severe eye problems.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet life at Green Gables in Avonlea with her brother Matthew. Wanting a boy to help Matthew with farm work, they sent word to adopt an orphan, but a mistake resulted in eleven-year-old Anne Shirley arriving instead. Though Marilla initially intended to return the girl, she softened upon realizing Anne's past neglect and agreed to keep her. She took charge of Anne's upbringing, instilling discipline, religious education, and proper behavior despite frequent trials caused by Anne's vivid imagination and quick temper. Over the next several years, Marilla grew deeply attached to Anne, taking pride in her academic success and personal growth. Following Matthew's sudden death from a heart attack caused by a bank failure, Marilla faced severe eye problems and considered selling Green Gables. However, Anne gave up her college scholarship to stay home and teach locally, allowing them to preserve their home. Marilla later took in her distant relative's orphaned twins, Davy and Dora Keith, and eventually arranged for her long-time friend Rachel Lynde to move into Green Gables to live with them.

She knew this must be Paul Irving and that Mrs. Rachel Lynde had been right for once when she prophesied that he would be unlike the Avonlea children. More than that, Anne realized that he was unlike other children anywhere, and that there was a soul subtly akin to her own gazing at her out of the very dark blue eyes that were watching her so intently.

His mouth was delicious, being full without pouting, the crimson lips just softly touching and curving into finely finished little corners that narrowly escaped being dimpled. Finding a kindred imaginative spirit in Anne, Miss Lavendar formed a warm friendship with the young girls, who began visiting her regularly. Through Anne, Miss Lavendar met Paul Irving, the son of her former fiancé Stephen Irving, and quickly grew attached to him. Learning of his son's visits, Stephen Irving returned to visit Miss Lavendar, leading to a reconciliation after twenty-five years apart. Following Matthew's sudden death from a heart attack caused by a bank failure, Marilla faced severe eye problems and considered selling Green Gables. However, Anne gave up her college scholarship to stay home and teach locally, allowing them to preserve their home. Marilla later took in her distant relative's orphaned twins, Davy and Dora Keith, and eventually arranged for her long-time friend Rachel Lynde to move into Green Gables to live with them.
